results.title: A Review of Recent Advanced Applications in Smart ...
results.content: To address the interdependence of these domains, Figure 2 presents a conceptual framework that integrates manufacturing technologies, system management, sustainability, and human–robot collaboration within SMSs. Manufacturing technologies provide the digital and physical infrastructure for intelligent operations; system management ensures coordination, optimisation, and decision-making; sustainability drives environmentally and economically viable practices; and human–robot collaboration enables collaboration, safety, and adaptability in hybrid workspaces. Over recent decades, continuous innovations across these technologies have accelerated the transition towards smart factories, where individual machines increasingly embed the principles of SMSs. These advancements are strongly linked to the integration of CPSs, DTs, and Artificial Intelligence (AI), which collectively enhance process monitoring, decision-making, and system-level optimisation [38]. Furthermore, the integration of DT technologies enables real-time forecasting of machine and process behaviours, enhancing predictive maintenance strategies and enabling dynamic control of manufacturing operations. This convergence underscores the growing role of intelligent modelling as a unifying principle in process parameter optimisation across machining, welding, additive manufacturing, and other advanced production systems.
